areas.title: Mindset & Discipline
areas.intro: Mindset and discipline. I care about the standard you keep when nobody claps. Name it, then we will practice keeping it.
areas.nudge: Say reflect to answer three short questions, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: Name one standard you kept this week, even when it was inconvenient.
reflections.reply: Good. A standard you can name is a standard you can keep.

reflections.prompt: Where did you negotiate that standard down, and what did it cost?
reflections.reply: That honesty is the work. We train the moment you want to slip.

reflections.prompt: What is the one rep you will not skip tomorrow?
reflections.reply: One clear rep. Do that before you negotiate with yourself.

areas.title: Health & Fitness
areas.intro: Health and fitness. Energy is the budget for every other goal. Tell me the truth about how you treated your body lately.
areas.nudge: Say reflect for a short check-in, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: How did your body feel over the last two days, in one honest sentence?
reflections.reply: I have that. We start from the body you actually have.

reflections.prompt: What did you do, or skip, that your future self would notice?
reflections.reply: Noted. Small skips compound, and so do small keeps.

reflections.prompt: What is one physical promise you can keep before tomorrow night?
reflections.reply: Make it small enough to finish. Then finish it.

areas.title: Career & Income
areas.intro: Career and income. Skill is how you stay expensive. We can drill Security Plus, or practice holding a room when someone cuts you off.
areas.nudge: Say Security Plus, say communication, or say reflect.

reflections.prompt: Which skill, if you were sharper at it in ninety days, would change your options?
reflections.reply: That is a real target. We will aim practice at it.

reflections.prompt: What did you practice this week that was uncomfortable and useful?
reflections.reply: Uncomfortable and useful is the right kind of work.

reflections.prompt: What will you study or ship in the next session?
reflections.reply: Say it once more in your head, then go do the first ten minutes.

areas.title: Business & Entrepreneurship
areas.intro: Business and entrepreneurship. Clarity is the product before the product. We will tighten who you serve and what you say.
areas.nudge: Say reflect, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: Who do you serve, and what problem do they already pay to solve?
reflections.reply: If you can say that cleanly, you can build on it.

reflections.prompt: What offer is still vague in your mouth? Say it in one sentence.
reflections.reply: Shorter is stronger. We will sand that sentence down next time.

reflections.prompt: What is the next conversation you need to have, and with whom?
reflections.reply: Put that conversation on the calendar. Thinking is not the same as asking.

areas.title: Relationships & Communication
areas.intro: Relationships and communication. Warmth and spine can live in the same sentence. We can walk the spice aisle, or practice staying calm when someone interrupts.
areas.nudge: Say social, say communication, or say reflect.

reflections.prompt: Think of a recent conversation that mattered. Did the other person feel included?
reflections.reply: Inclusion is a skill, not a mood. We can practice it.

reflections.prompt: Where did you talk to impress, instead of to connect?
reflections.reply: Catching that in the moment is most of the correction.

reflections.prompt: What is one question you wish you had asked?
reflections.reply: Keep that question. Use it in the next real conversation.

areas.title: Real Estate & Investing
areas.intro: Real estate and investing. Fall in love with the numbers before the photos. We will separate what you know from what you are guessing.
areas.nudge: Say reflect for three questions, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: If a property had to support your life, what would it need to produce each month?
reflections.reply: A number turns a dream into a screen.

reflections.prompt: What do you actually understand about how that asset makes money, and what are you still guessing?
reflections.reply: Guesses are fine if you label them. We will replace them with facts.

reflections.prompt: What fact will you learn before you get attached to a deal?
reflections.reply: Learn that fact first. Attachment can wait.

areas.title: Lifestyle & Experiences
areas.intro: Lifestyle and experiences. A good life is chosen, not performed. Tell me what actually restored you, and what only looked good.
areas.nudge: Say reflect, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: Which experience this month actually restored you, and which one only looked good?
reflections.reply: Keep the one that restored you. Let the performance go.

reflections.prompt: What are you spending time on that you would not defend out loud?
reflections.reply: If you would not defend it, it does not deserve the calendar.

reflections.prompt: What is one experience worth planning, not posting?
reflections.reply: Plan it quietly. Anticipation is part of the gift.

areas.title: Spirituality & Purpose
areas.intro: Spirituality and purpose. Purpose is what you refuse to betray. We will see whether your week agreed with your answer.
areas.nudge: Say reflect, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: What are you unwilling to betray, even if it slows you down?
reflections.reply: Hold that line. Speed is not the same as direction.

reflections.prompt: Where did your calendar disagree with that answer this week?
reflections.reply: The calendar tells the truth. We can edit it.

reflections.prompt: What practice, however small, will you keep tomorrow?
reflections.reply: Small and kept beats grand and imagined.

areas.title: Current Affairs
areas.summary: Fact, opinion, and the missing view.
areas.intro: Current affairs. We practice on a story this device actually fetched. If the feed is quiet, I say so and we drill the skill. I will not invent a headline.
areas.nudge: Start Current Affairs, or name another area.

reflections.prompt: What is one sentence you heard this week that mixed a fact with a judgment?
reflections.reply: Good. Split them. The fact can stay. The judgment needs a label.

reflections.prompt: Who was not in that sentence, and what might they have cared about?
reflections.reply: That missing person is the other perspective. Keep them in the room.

reflections.prompt: What would you need from a source before you repeated the story?
reflections.reply: A source and a date. Without those, it is not ready to repeat.
